advisory.finding: P11 ac-vagueness makes previously-advisory, broad subjective terms (good, nice, optimal, efficient, better) HARD-BLOCK a plan by default when they appear on any AC checklist line. These were advisory-only under the old P6 lexicon; promoting them to a default block is a substantial behavior change whose safety rests entirely on an unreproducible '0 FPs across 304 plans' backtest claim, and terms like 'good'/'efficient' can legitimately appear in a concrete AC (e.g. 'returns 200 for a good request', 'the O(n) path is efficient').

det_clarity.py:47 `_CODE_SPAN_RE = re.compile(r"`[^`\n]+`")` matches any backtick token, not only a proving command

advisory.finding: P10 accepts ANY inline code span in an AC item as proof of verification (`_CODE_SPAN_RE.search(it)`), so an AC that merely names a config/symbol in backticks (e.g. '- [ ] the `feature_flag` is set') passes the blocking verification-presence check without naming any verification. This makes P10 weaker than its stated intent for a blocking check.

advisory.finding: Two new DET checks p10_verification_presence and p11_ac_vagueness are added as UNCONDITIONALLY-blocking floor checks (blocking=True) with no opt-in/version flag and no disabled_builtins-style opt-out in run_det_floor, so plans that the gate previously ACCEPTED are now BLOCKED — an unversioned behavior/config backward-compat break for existing repos using the plan-review gate. A leaf plan with no `## Testing`/`## Verification` section and no code-span/verification-vocabulary AC item now hard-blocks (P10); any AC item containing a fixed-lexicon vague term now hard-blocks (P11).
scenarios: An existing repo re-runs review-plan on a leaf ticket whose ACs name no proving command and lacks a ## Testing section: previously PASS, now BLOCKED by P10
An existing plan whose AC says 'reasonable performance' or 'works properly': previously advisory (P6), now hard-BLOCKED by P11
